answer: The challenge noted regarding holding private actors responsible for AI existential risks under international human rights law is that the current legal framework primarily places obligations solely on state actors. This reflects the vertical nature of international human rights law, where states are considered the predominant oppressive power and are responsible for human rights obligations. As a result, private actors are not under any legal obligation to take precautions to address AI as an existential threat, although there is some movement towards recognizing private actors being subjected to human rights obligations. However, this recognition has not yet emerged as a matter of international law.
